title: Erasmus+ MotivAction: second stage of the transnational project in Moldova
body_html:
ActivAction in support of honest sport.

In March 2024, the second stage of the ActivAction project took place. It began with joint sessions with coaches, referees and athletes from various sports to introduce the whistleblowing platform, build and engage an integrity community, and apply abuse-reporting policies at national level.

The project coordinator, Corentin Segalen, and EU integrity investigator Massimiliano Michenzi brought international expertise to the sessions, focusing on implementing the Macolin Convention and developing cooperation on integrity in sport. The PNIS discussed the practical and operational aspects of making the platform work more effectively.

Key points of the MotivAction action plan:

- strengthening the Integrity Network;

- appointing an integrity delegate in 4 federations/associations: basketball, football, tennis and table tennis;

- creating an integrity community to analyse and discuss the situations encountered.

Communication and awareness campaign

Creating and displaying awareness posters at strategic sports venues.

A clear reporting procedure

Promoting the use of the secure website of the Moldovan Anti-Doping Agency (ANAD), which can also be reached through the official page attp.md.

Coaches’ and athletes’ compliance with professional ethics will continue to be monitored by the members of a national platform for ensuring integrity in sport. The new body will be set up by the Ministry of Education and Research with the support of development partners.

The topic was also discussed by Council of Europe experts Corentin Segalen and Patrick Vajda with the President of the International Federation of Sports Officials (IFSO), Artiom Jucov, the director of the National Anti-Doping Agency and the State Secretary of the Ministry of Education and Research, Sergiu Gurin. As a reminder, in 2018 the Republic of Moldova ratified the Council of Europe Convention on the Manipulation of Sports Competitions (the Macolin Convention), which requires ensuring integrity in sport and respect for the professional ethics of coaches and athletes. The Convention is the only binding international legal framework that provides for preventing, detecting and sanctioning manipulation in sport, promoting information exchange and cooperation between the public authorities involved, sports organisations and betting operators.

The MotivAction project demonstrates the Republic of Moldova’s commitment to fighting the manipulation of sports competitions and promoting integrity in sport through international cooperation and concrete measures.
